Shri K. K. Tiwari, Government Advocate for the respond
None for the complainant, though served.
Heard on I.A. No.8299/2022, which is first application filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant - Harisingh Beldar.

Learned Trial Court has convicted the appellant under Sections 450, 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 376(3)
of IPC alongwith 5 (j-ii)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced him to undergo RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.7,000/-, RI for 07 years with fine of Rs.7,000/-, RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.7,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.7,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.7,000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.7,000/- respectively with default stipulations,
vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 18.08.2021 passed by the 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Biaora, District Rajgarh in S.T. No.247/2019.
As per prosecution case, at the time of incident, prosecutrix (PW-1) was aged about 15 years 10 months.

sentences.text: During the period 14.06.2019 to 17.06.2019, appellant had kidnapped the prosecutrix and repeatedly committed rape upon her.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

Parents of the prosecutrix have not deposed the exact date of birth of prosecutrix therefore, learned Trial Court has wrongly assessed the age of the prosecutrix only on the basis of scholar register.
Appellant was implicated in the case due to enmity.
MLC report does not support the case of the prosecution.
Appellant is in custody since June, 2019.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence may be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submits that prosecutrix has supported the case of the prosecution and her statement is further supported by FSL report (Exhibit- P/17) and DNA report (Exhibit-P/21) therefore, it is prayed that the application for suspension of jail sentence is liable to be rejected.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Considering the statement of prosecutrix (PW-1), at this stage, we are not inclined to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.
IA No.8299/2022 is accordingly rejected.
In view of aforesaid, IA No.8300/2022, which is an application for urgent hearing stands disposed of.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
